questions.question: Which component of Node.js provides the event loop and asynchronous I/O?
questions.explanation: V8 executes JavaScript; libuv is the C library that implements the event loop, non-blocking I/O and the thread pool.

questions.question: Node is often called single-threaded. Which statement is most accurate?
options: Your JavaScript runs on one main thread, but libuv uses a thread pool (default 4 threads) for work like file system calls and some crypto
Node runs every request on its own operating system thread
Node has no threads at all, including inside V8
Node can only handle one network connection at a time
questions.explanation: Only one JavaScript callback runs at a time on the main thread, but fs, dns.lookup, pbkdf2/scrypt and zlib use the libuv thread pool, and V8 uses background threads too.

questions.question: Which workload is Node.js least suited to running on its main thread?
options: A JSON REST API that mostly waits on a database
A reverse proxy forwarding HTTP requests
A long-running image-processing calculation done in plain JavaScript
questions.explanation: CPU-bound work blocks the single main thread and stalls every other request; I/O-bound work is where Node shines. Heavy computation belongs in worker threads or separate processes.

questions.question: Which Node release line is the usual recommendation for production?
options: Any release that has reached end-of-life, because it is stable
Whatever version happens to be installed globally
questions.explanation: Active LTS releases receive bug and security fixes for a long period; Current releases are for trying new features, and end-of-life releases get no security fixes.
